hook: For the first time, prime editing is rewriting DNA inside a patient's body.
sections: Prime Medicine has treated the first person in a trial for Wilson's disease.
Think of a book editor. Older tools could only swap one letter for another. Prime editing is a full editor that can insert, delete and rewrite words in place.
First, the editor is delivered to liver cells. Second, it rewrites the faulty DNA so the cells can clear excess copper again.
Before, no in-body gene-editing therapy was approved, and base editing could not fix the most common Wilson's mutations.
Now a patient has been dosed, and first results are expected next year.
If results hold, Prime Medicine, ticker PRME, gains a first-in-class story. Early, single trial. Our judgment: small bet. Not financial advice.
